Method source: Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower, 'The Polar Express: Optimal Matrix Sign Methods and Their Application to the Muon Algorithm' (2025): per-iteration minimax-optimal odd-quintic coefficients with a 1.01 spectral-norm safety factor; shown stable in bf16 and improving GPT-2-scale Muon validation loss at equal iteration count versus the fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) quintic.
expected_effect: val_bpb DECREASES by 0.001-0.003 at an unchanged step count (2071 +/- 1% vs trn21 control 1.005734). Predeclared: candidate <= 1.0037 at 2050-2100 steps = win; 1.0037-1.0057 = null (tie goes to incumbent); > 1.0057 = negative. Step count outside 2050-2100 is a throughput anomaly and voids the BPB read.
hypothesis: Muon's orthogonalization currently uses MUON_NS_STEPS=5 Newton-Schulz iterations with one fixed quintic coefficient triple (3 matmuls each; train.py ~line 416). Replacing that fixed triple with the per-iteration optimal 'Polar Express' coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; the same 5-iteration schedule adopted in modded-nanogpt) yields a substantially closer approximation to the polar factor UV^T at the SAME matmul count, so each Muon update is closer to the intended orthogonal direction (less shrinkage of small singular directions, less spurious amplification). Because the op count, shapes and dtypes of the NS loop are unchanged, step time is unchanged (steps should land at ~2071 like both controls), so any BPB delta is a pure per-step-quality delta and cannot be step-count confounded. Predicted: lower val_bpb at equal steps.

When True, the Newton-Schulz orthogonalization used by MuonAdamW's Muon step (a) divides the input by (frobenius_norm * 1.01 + eps) instead of (frobenius_norm + eps) and (b) uses, at iteration i (0-based), the i-th coefficient triple from the fixed Polar Express table below instead of the single quintic triple, for the same MUON_NS_STEPS iterations, same matmul structure (A = X X^T; B = b*A + c*A@A; X = a*X + B@X), same dtype, same tall-matrix transposition and same post-NS scaling. When False the code path is bit-identical to 9a4caa7b. Nothing else changes: no precision flag, no kernel flag, no architecture change, no LR/momentum/weight-decay change, no data/evaluator change.
